claims.title: Why does the graph preserve the pairing and split the Lie quotient?

claims.statement: The graph is isotropic and the distinguished eigenspace on its quotient decomposes into labelled character eigenspaces.

claims.title: How does the Hodge graph give an abelian scheme with an action of the order?
claims.hypotheses: The special object is an abelian variety over the residue field, and its dual crystalline Hodge lift is an order-stable split filtration over the dual numbers with their square-zero divided powers.
claims.statement: The chosen filtration is realized by an abelian scheme with a lift of the full order action.

claims.title: Why does the polarization lift, and what happens to its degree?

claims.statement: The polarization correspondence lifts to the same abelian scheme, with its symmetry, compatibility and prescribed kernel condition.

claims.title: Which first-order coefficient is intrinsic to the marked deformation?
claims.hypotheses: The degree-one unitary moduli scheme is smooth over the prescribed mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring. The principal level is at least three and prime to q and the geometric point lies above a component generic point.
claims.statement: The two coefficients of lifts of x in the same filtration must coincide in H/Fil. Under the longer local branch they are b outside Fil and zero, proving the generic count Q^(n−1).
